Convert antimicrobial names, AMR codes or ATC codes to BNF codes

Source: R/crosswalk.R
ab_to_bnf.Rd

Looks up each input in the bundled antibiotic_crosswalk and returns the matching BNF chemical substance code(s). Inputs can be:

Usage

ab_to_bnf(
  x,
  scope = c("systemic", "all"),
  output = c("table", "codes"),
  use_amr = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

Character vector of names or codes.

scope

"systemic" (default) keeps BNF chapter 5 (infections: oral and injectable products). "all" also returns topical, eye, ear, skin and vaginal chemicals from chapters 7, 11, 12 and 13, which are prescribed for different purposes and should not be pooled with systemic use by accident.

output

"table" (default) returns one row per input and BNF chemical; "codes" returns the unique BNF chemical codes as a character vector.

use_amr

Use AMR::as.ab() for inputs the bundled table cannot resolve (default TRUE; ignored if AMR is not installed).

Value

A data frame with columns input, ab, ab_name, atc, bnf_chemical_code, bnf_name, bnf_section and via (how the input was recognised: "bundled table" or "AMR::as.ab"), or a character vector of codes if output = "codes". Inputs that cannot be resolved, or that resolve to an agent with no BNF chemical in scope, give a warning (naming the agent, so fuzzy matches are visible) and a row with NA codes. Group and class inputs silently skip members that have no BNF chemical in scope.

Details

  • AMR package antimicrobial codes ("AMX"),

  • antimicrobial names as used by AMR or the BNF ("amoxicillin", "Co-amoxiclav"),

  • full ATC codes ("J01CA04") or ATC prefixes that select a whole class ("J01CA" = aminopenicillins, "J01M" = quinolones),

  • AMR antimicrobial group names ("Penicillins", "Carbapenems"),

  • anything else, if the AMR package is installed: free text, synonyms and brand names are resolved with AMR::as.ab().

Note

Matches made by AMR::as.ab() can be fuzzy; check the via column and ab_name.

See also

bnf_to_ab(), atc_to_bnf(), op_antibiotics()

Examples

ab_to_bnf(c("amoxicillin", "AMC", "J01XE01"))
#>         input  ab                     ab_name     atc bnf_chemical_code
#> 1 amoxicillin AMX                 Amoxicillin J01CA04         0501013B0
#> 2 amoxicillin AMX                 Amoxicillin J01CA04         0501013C0
#> 3         AMC AMC Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid J01CR02         0501013K0
#> 4     J01XE01 NIT              Nitrofurantoin J01XE01         0501130R0
#>                                     bnf_name bnf_section           via
#> 1                                Amoxicillin        0501 bundled table
#> 2                         Amoxicillin sodium        0501 bundled table
#> 3 Co-amoxiclav (Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid)        0501 bundled table
#> 4                             Nitrofurantoin        0501 bundled table
ab_to_bnf("doxycycline", output = "codes")
#> [1] "0501030I0" "0501030Z0"
# a whole class by ATC prefix, or by AMR group name
ab_to_bnf("J01MA", output = "codes")
#> [1] "0501120L0" "0501120P0" "0501120Q0" "0501120X0" "0501120Y0"
ab_to_bnf("Aminoglycosides", output = "codes")
#> [1] "0501040H0" "0501040U0"
# include topical / ophthalmic products
ab_to_bnf("chloramphenicol", scope = "all")
#>             input  ab         ab_name     atc bnf_chemical_code        bnf_name
#> 1 chloramphenicol CHL Chloramphenicol J01BA01         0501070F0 Chloramphenicol
#> 2 chloramphenicol CHL Chloramphenicol J01BA01         1103010C0 Chloramphenicol
#> 3 chloramphenicol CHL Chloramphenicol J01BA01         1201010H0 Chloramphenicol
#>   bnf_section           via
#> 1        0501 bundled table
#> 2        1103 bundled table
#> 3        1201 bundled table
